facts.content: Patient reports feeling really anxious for the past few months.
facts.source_text: CC: “Really anxious past few months”

facts.content: Anxiety onset approximately 2 months ago after starting a new job at a fashion-retail HQ; boss is harsh leading to daily dread of work.
facts.source_text: Onset ~2 mo, began after starting new fashion-retail HQ job; boss harsh → daily dread of work

facts.content: Symptoms include morning anxiety, reluctance to leave the house, palpitations lasting a few to 10 minutes, sleep-onset insomnia with 3 to 4 hours of sleep per night, early waking with racing heart, daytime fatigue, anhedonia, decreased socializing, and cessation of running and tennis.
facts.source_text: Symptoms: morning anxiety, reluctance to leave house, palpitations (irregular, few–10 min), shallow sleep (sleep‐onset insomnia; 3–4 h/night), early waking with racing heart, daytime fatigue, anhedonia, ↓ socialising, stopped running/tennis

facts.content: No panic attacks have occurred to date, but there is a fear of escalation.
facts.source_text: No panic attacks to date; fears escalation

facts.content: Mood is low but denies suicidal ideation.

facts.content: Work-related anxiety or generalized anxiety disorder with secondary insomnia and palpitations.

facts.content: Palpitations are likely anxiety-related, but organic causes such as thyroid issues or anemia should be excluded.
facts.source_text: 2. Palpitations likely anxiety-related; organic causes to exclude (thyroid, anemia, etc.)

facts.content: Provide self-referral link to NHS talking therapy (CBT).
facts.source_text: Provide self-referral link to NHS talking therapy (CBT)

facts.content: Offer online anxiety resources and add sleep hygiene advice.

facts.content: Order basic blood panel (FBC, TFT, U&E) to screen for reversible causes of palpitations.
facts.source_text: Order basic blood panel (FBC, TFT, U&E) to screen for reversible causes of palpitations

facts.content: Arrange GP review 1 week after blood tests to discuss results and progress.

facts.content: Advise patient to call back if symptoms worsen or daily function is impaired.

facts.content: Discuss possibility of anxiolytic or pharmacotherapy if non-pharmacological measures prove inadequate.
